novedades.texto: MRS (11 items): somatic, psychological, urogenital. Heinemann 2004 scheme (HQLO 2:67; total and by domain, the one CaVeSal® adopts): total 0-4 no/little symptoms · 5-8 mild · 9-15 moderate · ≥16 severe (consider HRT); somatic 0-2 · 3-4 · 5-7 · ≥8; psychological 0-1 · 2-3 · 4-6 · ≥7; urogenital 0 · 1 · 2-3 · ≥4. Variant from the methodological review (HQLO 2:45, Table 6): total moderate 9-16 / severe ≥17 and somatic moderate 5-8 / severe ≥9 (psychological and urogenital the same). SOCHEG scheme (broken down by domain, each with its own severe-alteration cutoff): Somatic (items 1-4) ≥8 · Psychological (items 5-8) ≥6 · Urogenital (items 9-11) ≥3 · Total (items 1-11) ≥15. HRT by uterine status: no uterus → estrogen alone. Uterus present, perimenopause → sequential/cyclic. Postmenopause → continuous combined. Transdermal HRT (preferred, especially with hypertension, obesity BMI>30, hypertriglyceridemia, VTE risk): 17β-Estradiol gel 0.75-1.25g/day, or patches 25-50mcg/day. Endometrial protection (intact uterus): Micronized natural progesterone 200mg/day for 10-14 days/month (sequential regimen) or 100mg/day continuous · or Dydrogesterone 10-20mg/day. Tibolone (STEAR): 2.5mg/day PO (or 1.25mg/day in lower body weight or advanced perimenopause) — covers vasomotor symptoms, urogenital atrophy and bone loss prevention (estrogen doses to prevent bone loss and what to do when MHT is stopped: see Osteoporosis and bone densitometry); does not require an added progestogen. Tissue-selective estrogen complex (alternative when avoiding a progestogen is preferred): Conjugated equine estrogens 0.45mg/day + Bazedoxifene 20mg/day — bazedoxifene (a SERM) replaces the progestogen for endometrial protection, without the bleeding or breast tenderness associated with it. Evidence from the SMART-1/SMART-2 trials (12 weeks): significant reduction in hot flush frequency/severity vs. placebo, with a 50% reduction by day 8-10 and a sustained ~90% reduction by day 83 of use; no increased risk of breast cancer, endometrial cancer, VTE, stroke or coronary disease in pooled analyses (follow-up up to 2 years — confidence limited by low event incidence and lack of longer-term data). ⚠️ Availability in Paraguay not confirmed — verify locally before prescribing. Alternative endometrial protection — 52mg LNG-IUD: off-label use alongside systemic estrogen to provide endometrial protection (plus contraception if applicable) — replace at 5 years when used for this purpose (the approved contraceptive lifespan is 8 years, but the evidence supporting endometrial protection in HRT covers up to 5 years). Local availability (Paraguay, confirm against the current pharmacy/distributor): transdermal 17β-estradiol gel/spray (e.g., Ginoderm) — available. 17β-estradiol vaginal ring — not available. Conjugated equine estrogens + bazedoxifene — availability unconfirmed. This information is contextual, to anticipate the availability conversation with the patient — it should not be used to exclude an option from the clinical list. Interaction with GLP-1/GIP agonists: the gastric emptying delay induced by semaglutide/tirzepatide (more pronounced with the latter) may reduce absorption of oral HRT — in patients on GLP-1/GIP therapy, prefer the transdermal route for estrogen therapy (same pharmacokinetic principle as in the Contraception during tirzepatide guide). Order of pharmacologic treatment for vasomotor symptoms (ACP 2026): 1st line — estrogen + progestogen with a uterus, or estrogen alone without a uterus (strong recommendation, high certainty). 2nd line, if contraindicated or not tolerated — SNRI: desvenlafaxine or venlafaxine. 3rd line — SSRI (escitalopram or paroxetine), gabapentin or NK antagonists (fezolinetant or elinzanetant): see Fezolinetant and elinzanetant. Shared decision: benefits, harms, comorbidities, preferences, cost and availability.

novedades.fuentes: WHO Semen Manual (6th ed., 2021) · WHO Infertility Guideline 2025 · AUA/ASRM 2024 · EAU
novedades.texto: WHO 2021 lower reference limits (5th percentile): volume 1.4 mL · concentration 16 M/mL · total 39 M per ejaculate · total motility 42 % · progressive 30 % · normal forms 4 % · vitality 54 %. Nomenclature: hypospermia (low volume) · oligozoospermia (low concentration or total) · asthenozoospermia (low progressive) · teratozoospermia (low normal forms) · necrozoospermia (low vitality) · OAT (all three) · cryptozoospermia (only in the centrifuged pellet) · azoospermia (none after centrifugation). Management: normal result: one test is enough. Abnormal: repeat after ≥11 weeks (WHO 2025) and refer to urology/andrology with physical exam, FSH and testosterone. Concentration <5 M/mL with high FSH or testicular atrophy: karyotype; ≤1 M/mL or non-obstructive azoospermia: Y-chromosome microdeletions (AUA/ASRM 2024). Azoospermia: volume, pH and FSH; absent vas deferens → CFTR testing. Low volume: post-ejaculatory urinalysis and rule out obstruction. TMSC (total motile sperm after processing) — CaVeSal® suggestion: >3–5 M → IUI · 1–3 M → IVF · <1 M → direct ICSI. Fewer than 5 M motile sperm after processing lowers IUI success (AUA/ASRM 2024). Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (Couple workup).

novedades.fuentes: Amor F et al. J Ultrasound Med 2009;28:285-291 · UOG 2011;38:450-455 · meta-analysis PubMed 36790399
novedades.texto: Categories: 1 normal ovaries (0 %) · 2 very probably benign, functional: follicle, corpus luteum, hemorrhagic cyst (<1 %) · 3 probably benign, non-functional: endometrioma, dermoid, simple cyst, hydrosalpinx, paraovarian cyst, inclusion cyst, pedunculated fibroid (1–4 %) · 4 probably malignant, one or two malignancy features (5–20 %) · 5 very probably malignant, three or more features (>20 %). Malignancy features: thick papillary projections, thick septa, solid areas, ascites, central vascularization, resistance index <0.5. Management: 1–2 no follow-up or follow-up; 3 general gynecologist; 4–5 markers (CA-125, CEA, AFP/hCG/LDH if <40), contrast MRI or CT as appropriate, and referral to gynecologic oncology. Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (Adnexal mass).

novedades.fuentes: ATA 2017 · Endocrine Society · Lazarus JH et al. NEJM 2012 (CATS) · Casey BM et al. NEJM 2017 · Dhillon-Smith RK et al. NEJM 2019 (TABLET)
novedades.texto: Anti-TPO+ (>34 IU/mL) + TSH above range: Hashimoto's, start levothyroxine. Anti-TPO+ with TSH 2.5–4.0: consider levothyroxine (ATA 2017). Anti-TPO+ with normal TSH: recheck every 4–6 wk (2–5x risk of gestational hypothyroidism). The TABLET trial (2019) showed no benefit of levothyroxine in euthyroid anti-TPO+ women. Preconception (ATA 2017): treated hypothyroid women, adjust to TSH between the lower limit and 2.5. IVF/ICSI with subclinical hypothyroidism: levothyroxine with a TSH goal <2.5 (rec. 20). Confirmed pregnancy on prior treatment: +25–30% starting dose. Neurodevelopment: CATS (2012) and Casey (2017) showed no benefit of treating subclinical hypothyroidism on child IQ. Anti-Tg: isolated positive anti-Tg also indicates thyroid autoimmunity, but the ATA 2017 levothyroxine decision is based on anti-TPO. With positive anti-Tg, check TSH once pregnancy is confirmed.

novedades.titulo: Ovulation induction — Cancellation criteria and OHSS prevention
novedades.fuentes: ESHRE Female Infertility Guideline (2023), Hum Reprod Open 2023(3):hoad034 · ASRM Practice Committee (2013), Fertil Steril 100:341-348
novedades.texto: In low-complexity techniques (timed intercourse/IUI), the safety threshold requires strictly avoiding high-order multiple pregnancy and Ovarian Hyperstimulation Syndrome (OHSS). Immediate cancellation criteria — do NOT give hCG: ≥3 mature follicles (≥15-16mm) in women <35 years, or >3-4 mature follicles in any low-complexity patient. More than 4-6 intermediate follicles (11-14mm) that could respond to the trigger. Serum estradiol >1,000-1,500pg/mL (if measured). Management on cancellation: cancel and withhold the hCG trigger (it is the direct trigger for the VEGF cascade and capillary hyperpermeability of OHSS). Advise strict coital abstinence or mandatory condom use for ≥7-10 days. Do not give hCG for luteal support. Rescue option at a high-complexity center: convert the cycle to IVF with follicular aspiration, GnRH-agonist trigger, and total embryo cryopreservation ("freeze-all").

novedades.titulo: Ovulation induction — Follicular size for the hCG trigger
novedades.fuentes: ASRM Practice Committee (2013), Fertil Steril 100:341-348 · ASRM Practice Committee (2020), Fertil Steril 113:66-70 · Palatnik et al. (2012), Fertil Steril 97:1089-1094 · Shalom-Paz et al. (2014), Gynecol Endocrinol 30(2):107-110 · Ling et al. (2024), Eur J Med Res 29:184 · Van Oirschot et al. (2025), Fertil Steril · ESHRE Ovarian Stimulation Guideline (2025) · ESHRE Female Infertility Guideline (2023), Hum Reprod Open 2023(3):hoad034
novedades.texto: The hCG trigger mimics the endogenous LH surge: it resumes oocyte meiosis, luteinizes the granulosa cells, and times follicular rupture (36-40h after administration). Trigger agents: Recombinant hCG (r-hCG) 250mcg SC · urinary hCG (u-hCG) 5,000-10,000 IU IM. Follicular size by inducing agent: Clomiphene citrate: trigger with the leading follicle at a mean diameter of 20-28mm; ASRM notes higher pregnancy rates at 23-28mm (follicles under clomiphene mature at larger diameters: in conception cycles the leading follicle measured 20.4 ± 1.2mm). Monitor endometrial thickness because of the antiestrogenic effect. Letrozole: trigger with the leading follicle at 19-23mm (optimal 19.1-21mm in the first IUI cycle); tolerated up to 28mm. Gonadotropins (FSH/hMG): trigger with the leading follicle at 16-18mm (oocyte maturity is reached at slightly smaller sizes under direct gonadotropins; triggering above 19-20mm increases oocyte senescence). Note: ESHRE (2025) considers that the association between follicle size and outcome has not been sufficiently studied; the trigger size is individualized. Concurrent endometrial status: ideally ≥7mm with a trilaminar pattern before ordering the trigger. Timing of intercourse/insemination: timed intercourse — the night of the trigger and again 36h later (or on alternating days: trigger day and the next). IUI — sperm preparation and insemination at 36h (range 34-38h) post-hCG.

novedades.titulo: Ovulation induction — Therapeutic choice: Letrozole vs. Clomiphene vs. Gonadotropins
novedades.fuentes: ASRM Practice Committee (2013), Fertil Steril 100:341-348 · Teede et al., Int'l PCOS Guideline (2023), Fertil Steril 120(4):767-793 · ESHRE Female Infertility Guideline (2023), Hum Reprod Open 2023(3):hoad034 · MSPyBS Paraguay (2025), Res. S.G. Nº 050/2025
novedades.texto: Letrozole (aromatase inhibitor) — first-line in PCOS/WHO Type II anovulation, especially with overweight/obesity (BMI≥25-30). Higher cumulative ovulation, clinical pregnancy and live-birth rates than clomiphene (PPCOS II trial). Does not block endometrial or cervical estrogen receptors (preserves endometrial thickness and cervical mucus quality). Short half-life (~48h): favors monofollicular development, lower multiple-pregnancy rate. Clomiphene citrate (SERM): first-line alternative when letrozole is unavailable/not tolerated, or in unexplained infertility (timed intercourse/IUI). Drawback: prolonged peripheral antiestrogenic effect (half-life >2 weeks) — refractory thin endometrium (<7mm) and hostile mucus; higher multifollicular/multiple-pregnancy rate (5-10%, mostly twins) than letrozole. Exogenous gonadotropins (recombinant FSH / hMG): failure or resistance to oral agents (after 3-6 ovulatory cycles without conception); or Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism (WHO Type I — hypothalamic-pituitary axis not intact, clomiphene/letrozole do NOT work, requires hMG or FSH+hCG/LH microdose); or as an adjunct in low-complexity/IUI cycles.

novedades.titulo: Ovulation induction — Dosing regimens and stimulation protocols
novedades.fuentes: ASRM Practice Committee (2013), Fertil Steril 100:341-348 · ESHRE Female Infertility Guideline (2023), Hum Reprod Open 2023(3):hoad034 · MSPyBS Paraguay (2025), Res. S.G. Nº 050/2025
novedades.texto: Letrozole: 2.5mg/day PO x5 days, starting cycle day 2-5. If no ovulation, escalate to 5.0mg/day the next cycle; maximum dose 7.5mg/day x5 days. Clomiphene citrate: 50mg/day PO x5 days, day 2-5. If no response, increase to 100mg/day; usual maximum 150mg/day x5 days (higher doses do not improve pregnancy rates and worsen the endometrial antiestrogenic effect). Limit: 6 ovulatory cycles. Gonadotropins — "Low-Dose Step-Up" protocol: strict goal of monofollicular development and OHSS prevention. Starting dose 37.5-50-75 IU/day SC/IM from cycle day 2-3, holding the fixed dose for 7-14 days. If after 14 days there is no follicular selection (no follicle ≥10mm), increase 50% weekly (e.g. 37.5→75 IU/day) until a response is seen, then maintain that dose through the trigger.

novedades.titulo: Ovulation induction — Treatment failure and drug resistance
novedades.fuentes: ASRM Practice Committee (2013), Fertil Steril 100:341-348
novedades.texto: Drug resistance: persistent absence of recruitment, or no follicles ≥15mm despite maximum doses. Clomiphene resistance: anovulation after 150mg/day x5 days. Letrozole resistance: anovulation after 7.5mg/day x5 days. Management: switch therapeutic line (CC→Letrozole, add Metformin in PCOS with insulin resistance, or move to low-dose gonadotropins). Failed induction (treatment failure): confirmed regular ovulatory cycles (optimal follicular development, follicular rupture and adequate luteal phase with progesterone ≥10ng/mL) without pregnancy after 4-6 consecutive ovulatory cycles. Management: full couple re-evaluation (tubal patency by HSG if not yet done, repeat semen analysis with TMSC) and escalation to high-complexity ART (IVF/ICSI). Endometrial failure (antiestrogenic effect): adequate follicular growth but persistently thin endometrium (<6-7mm) in the preovulatory window (common with clomiphene). Management: switch to letrozole or add exogenous estrogen support.

novedades.titulo: Ovulation induction — Baseline and serial ultrasound monitoring
novedades.fuentes: ASRM Practice Committee (2013), Fertil Steril 100:341-348 · ESHRE Female Infertility Guideline (2023), Hum Reprod Open 2023(3):hoad034
novedades.texto: Baseline transvaginal ultrasound + Antral Follicle Count (AFC), cycle days 2-4 — mandatory before starting any inducing agent: thin, shed endometrium (<5mm); rule out functional cysts/persistent follicles from the previous cycle (start if no follicles/cysts >10mm; postpone/cancel if a residual cyst or growing follicle ≥10-15mm is found, usually with baseline E2 >50-60pg/mL). AFC (bilateral 2-9mm follicles): <5-7 suggests low ovarian reserve · 8-15 normal reserve · ≥20 (or ovarian volume ≥10mL) polycystic ovarian morphology — maximum alert for hyperresponse and OHSS risk. Serial follow-up: first post-stimulation scan on cycle day 8-10, then every 48-72h depending on follicular growth rate (expected physiologic growth 1.5-2mm/day). Record the mean diameter in 2 perpendicular planes per ovary, and endometrial thickness/pattern (optimal: periovulatory trilaminar "triple line" ≥7-8mm).

novedades.titulo: Insulin resistance — HOMA-IR and OGTT in PMOS
novedades.fuentes: Matthews DR et al. Diabetologia 1985 · International PMOS Guideline 2023 (Teede) · ADA Standards of Care
novedades.texto: HOMA-IR = fasting glucose (mg/dL) × fasting insulin (µU/mL) / 405 (with glucose in mmol/L: / 22.5). Limitations: there is no universal cut-off; it varies by population, BMI and insulin assay. The 2023 international guideline does not recommend measuring insulin or insulin resistance indices in routine clinical practice. Use it only as descriptive data. Recommended (2023 guideline): assess glycemic status at diagnosis and every 1–3 years; 75 g OGTT in every woman with PMOS planning pregnancy or fertility treatment (if not feasible, fasting glucose or HbA1c). Outside pregnancy (ADA): fasting 100–125 mg/dL impaired fasting glucose, ≥126 diabetes; 2 h 140–199 impaired tolerance, ≥200 diabetes; HbA1c 5.7–6.4 % prediabetes, ≥6.5 % diabetes. Management: lifestyle for all; metformin in adults with BMI ≥25 for metabolic outcomes; the 2023 guideline considers inositol experimental (see "Myo-inositol"). Lipid profile and blood pressure. Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (PMOS).

novedades.fuentes: ACR 2020 Reproductive Health Guideline (Sammaritano LR et al.) · SMFM Consult #64
novedades.texto: Timing: plan pregnancy with inactive or low-activity lupus for at least 6 months on compatible medication. Postpone after recent severe activity or severe organ damage. Prior labs: antiphospholipid antibodies (lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin, anti-β2 glycoprotein I) and anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB; renal function and proteinuria. Medication (ACR 2020): continue or start hydroxychloroquine. Stop mycophenolate ≥6 weeks before, methotrexate 1–3 months before and cyclophosphamide 3 months before. Compatible: hydroxychloroquine, azathioprine, tacrolimus, cyclosporine and low-dose prednisone. Low-dose aspirin from the first trimester, ideally from 12 weeks, for preeclampsia risk. Positive anti-Ro/La: risk of congenital heart block; fetal rhythm surveillance per protocol. With APS: see "Antiphospholipid Syndrome (APS) and thrombophilias". Team: counseling with maternal-fetal medicine and rheumatology before trying to conceive. Flagged in CaVeSal® GYN (Preconception).

novedades.fuentes: ACOG PB 171 · FIGO/WHO · NICE NG25
novedades.texto: Cutoffs by guideline: ACOG wk 24-33+6 (late 34-36+6) · FIGO/WHO 24-34+6 · NICE offer 24-33+6, consider 34-35+6. Regimens: Betamethasone 12mg IM q24h (2 doses) · Dexamethasone 6mg IM q12h (4 doses). Rescue course: if >14 days have passed, GA <34 wk, imminent risk within 7 days. In PROM, ACOG considers the evidence insufficient for or against: it may be considered, without delaying delivery.

novedades.titulo: Mammography and BI-RADS — Categories 4-6 and management
novedades.fuentes: ACR BI-RADS v2025 · ACOG PB 223 · ACR 2023 (high risk)
novedades.texto: BI-RADS 4 (>2-<95%): 4A (>2-≤10%) · 4B (>10-≤50%) · 4C (>50-<95%). Image-guided core needle biopsy with radiologic-pathologic concordance; discordant → repeat or surgical biopsy. 4A benign concordant: follow-up at 6 months. BI-RADS 5 (≥95%): spiculated mass, fine pleomorphic branching calcifications → biopsy and referral to breast surgery and oncology; staging (see Breast cancer — TNM staging). BI-RADS 6: proven malignancy → multidisciplinary team. High risk (BRCA, chest radiation before 30, lifetime risk ≥20 %): annual contrast MRI plus mammography.

novedades.titulo: Mammography and BI-RADS — Breast density and categories 0-3
novedades.fuentes: ACR BI-RADS v2025 · ACR Appropriateness Criteria (palpable mass) · ACOG PB 223/179 · USPSTF 2024 · FDA MQSA 2024
novedades.texto: Supplemental ultrasound: dense breasts (ACR C/D) according to risk, <30 years with palpable mass, cyst vs. solid. Density (ACR): A (fatty) · B (scattered) · C (heterogeneously dense) · D (extremely dense). C and D: notify the patient (FDA 2024); supplemental imaging by risk (ACR suggests it; USPSTF 2024: insufficient evidence). BI-RADS v2025 — category 0 split: 0 needs additional imaging → <30 years targeted ultrasound; ≥30 diagnostic mammography or tomosynthesis plus ultrasound · 0 needs prior studies → obtain them for comparison. 1 negative and 2 benign (0%): routine screening every 2 years from 40 to 74 (USPSTF 2024). 3 probably benign (>0-≤2%): follow-up at 6, 12 and 24 months; biopsy if it changes. Suspicious palpable mass with negative imaging: consider biopsy. Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (Breast, cervix and endometrium).

novedades.fuentes: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee. Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026. Diabetes Care. 2026 · NICE Guideline NG3. Diabetes in pregnancy · Rowan JA, Hague WM, Gao W, et al. (MiG Trial). N Engl J Med. 2008;358(19):2003-2015 · Rowan JA, et al. (MiG TOFU, offspring follow-up at 2 and 7-9 years). Diabetes Care 2011 / BMJ Open Diabetes Res Care 2018 · ADA/ALAD (see Gestational Diabetes guide)
novedades.texto: The approach to metformin once pregnancy is confirmed depends on why it was prescribed — it is not a single rule: PMOS with ovulation induction/insulin resistance: ADA 2026 (recommendation 15.22, level A): when metformin was used for PCOS and ovulation induction, stop it by the end of the first trimester at the latest. Many of these patients reach pregnancy already on metformin and/or myo-inositol as part of their baseline metabolic management (see the PMOS and Myo-inositol guides) — there is no teratogenicity signal for metformin requiring its immediate discontinuation upon confirming pregnancy, unlike GLP-1/GIP analogues (see the Inadvertent pregnancy guide). Prediabetes: individualize according to glycemic control and risk factors. ADA (2026 Standards of Care) does not position metformin as routine in isolated gestational prediabetes — its use follows the same individualization logic as in non-pregnant high-risk patients (elevated BMI, prior GDM, PMOS). NICE (NG3) is somewhat more permissive when risk factors for frank gestational diabetes coexist, where metformin may be anticipated as part of early management if glycemia warrants it — neither guideline indicates it routinely in isolated prediabetes without another risk factor. ADA 2026: metformin does not prevent gestational diabetes (meta-analysis of 11 RCTs). NICE NG3 (1.1.21): metformin may be used as an adjunct or alternative to insulin before and during pregnancy when the glycemic benefit outweighs potential harm. Pregestational diabetes: ADA prioritizes insulin as first-choice treatment (type 1 and, in most cases, type 2) due to metformin's transplacental passage and a preference for more predictable control; it reserves metformin as an adjunct in type 2 diabetes with high insulin resistance/high requirements, not as monotherapy. NICE (NG3) accepts metformin as first-line or adjunctive therapy in pregestational type 2 diabetes, adding insulin if the glycemic target is not reached — a stance more favorable to oral therapy than ADA's. Gestational diabetes: metformin as a second-line agent versus insulin per ADA (insulin as the preferred first line, metformin as an acceptable alternative after discussing transplacental passage with the patient); NICE (NG3) accepts metformin as a reasonable first line before insulin, barring contraindication or lack of response — see also the algorithm already described in the Gestational Diabetes guide. Summary of the ADA vs. NICE divergence: both agree that uncontrolled hyperglycemia, not metformin, is the real teratogen, but they differ in how much weight they give oral metformin versus insulin: ADA tends to favor insulin as first-line therapy in overt diabetes (pregestational and gestational), reserving metformin as an adjunct or an alternative discussed case by case; NICE accepts metformin more broadly as a reasonable first line in several scenarios. Neither guideline diverges on PMOS, where the decision is individualized for reasons unrelated to fetal safety. Key counseling point: the demonstrated teratogen in this context is uncontrolled hyperglycemia — not metformin itself. This should guide the decision not to abruptly stop an antidiabetic agent without an already-defined replacement plan (insulin or another scheme). Offspring follow-up (MiG TOFU): follow-up of the MiG trial children at 2 years (Diabetes Care 2011) and 7-9 years (BMJ Open Diabetes Res Care 2018) assessed body composition and metabolic outcomes after in-utero metformin exposure — with no signal of harm that would contraindicate its use in gestational diabetes; this is the longest-term support available for this specific indication.

novedades.titulo: Myo-inositol — PMOS, ovulation induction, and inadvertent exposure
novedades.fuentes: Facchinetti F, et al. Reduction of oocyte quality and clinical outcomes using myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol: an update, Expert Opin Drug Metab Toxicol (2020) · Unfer V, et al. Myo-inositol effects in women with PCOS: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials, Endocr Connect (2017) · Cochrane: Inositol for subfertility associated with PCOS (Review, 2023 update) · ESHRE/ASRM/Monash PCOS Guideline (2023) · Poyatos-León R, et al. The effect of myo-inositol supplementation on gestational diabetes mellitus prevention: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Am J Obstet Gynecol. 2026;235(5):1024-1036. DOI 10.1016/j.ajog.2026.05.020 · Motuhifonua SK, et al. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2023;CD011507.pub3
novedades.texto: Mechanism: myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol are second messengers in the insulin signaling pathway — supplementation improves ovarian insulin sensitivity, reduces compensatory hyperinsulinemia, and thereby favors resumption of ovulatory cycles in PMOS. It is not a drug in the strict sense but a dietary nutrient/supplement, which shapes its reproductive safety profile (see the inadvertent exposure note below). Indication: ovulatory dysfunction in PMOS/metabolic phenotype, as an adjunct or alternative to metformin in patients with digestive intolerance to the latter; also used as an adjuvant in ovulation induction/IVF protocols to improve oocyte quality. Dose: the 2023 international PCOS guideline (Teede et al., practice point 4.7.4) states that specific types, doses or combinations of inositol cannot be recommended for lack of evidence, and considers it experimental in infertility (5.8.1). Trials often used 2-4 g/day of myo-inositol, sometimes with D-chiro-inositol 40:1, but that regimen comes from studies, not a guideline-recommended dose. If prescribed, agree on it with the patient according to her preferences and reassess at 3-6 months. Evidence: the Cochrane review (2023 update) on inositol for PMOS-associated subfertility finds low-to-moderate certainty evidence favoring a possible improvement in clinical pregnancy and ovulation rates versus placebo, with meta-analyses by Unfer et al. and Facchinetti et al. also showing benefit on metabolic parameters (HOMA-IR, androgen profile) — overall evidence quality remains limited by study size and heterogeneity. Inadvertent exposure during fertility recovery (relevant in women coming off tirzepatide/semaglutide who are improving their metabolic profile): as a physiological nutrient normally present in the diet rather than a synthetic molecule with dedicated teratogenicity studies, myo-inositol is not subject to the same preconception washout restrictions as GLP-1/GIP analogues — no teratogenic warning signal has been described with continued use during an unrecognized pregnancy, and it has in fact also been studied as a supplement for gestational diabetes prevention in at-risk populations. This does not exempt confirming the pregnancy and reassessing the overall therapeutic plan as soon as it is detected. Specific meta-analysis on myo-inositol and gestational diabetes prevention (Poyatos-León R, et al. Am J Obstet Gynecol. 2026;235(5):1024-1036. DOI 10.1016/j.ajog.2026.05.020): 12 randomized controlled trials, 4,765 women without preexisting diabetes (pregnant or planning conception within 6 months), search through April 2025. Myo-inositol supplementation substantially reduced the risk of gestational diabetes versus control (44% relative risk reduction), with no significant differences in hypertensive disorders, cesarean delivery, macrosomia, preterm birth, or neonatal hypoglycemia. Cochrane review on prevention of gestational diabetes (Motuhifonua et al. 2023, CD011507.pub3): 7 RCTs with 1,319 women overall; gestational diabetes in 6 RCTs with 1,140 (RR 0.53; 95% CI 0.31-0.90; very low certainty); hypertensive disorders in 5 RCTs with 1,052 (RR 0.34; 95% CI 0.19-0.61; low certainty). ⚠️ Cochrane shows a reduction in hypertensive disorders and Poyatos-León finds no difference: the hypertensive finding is not conclusive.

novedades.fuentes: FIGO PALM-COEIN (Munro MG et al. IJGO 2018) · STEP-W (Lasmar 2011; ISGE 2023) · ACOG PB 228 (2021) · ASRM 2017
novedades.texto: Type 0 pedunculated intracavitary · 1 sessile <50% intramural · 2 sessile ≥50% · 3 100% intramural (contacts endometrium) · 4 100% intramural (no contact) · 5 subserosal ≥50% · 6 subserosal <50% · 7 pedunculated subserosal · 8 other locations · 2-5 transmural. STEP-W (submucosal): size ≤2 / >2–5 / >5 cm = 0/1/2 · topography lower/middle/upper third = 0/1/2 · base ≤1/3, >1/3–2/3, >2/3 of the wall = 0/1/2 · penetration 0 / ≤50 % / >50 % = 0/1/2 · lateral wall +1. Group I (0–4) low complexity · II (5–6) complex: prior GnRH analogues or two-step surgery · III (7–9) alternatives to hysteroscopy. Management: asymptomatic, expectant. Symptomatic submucosal: hysteroscopic myomectomy. Types 3–5: medical treatment (LNG-IUS, GnRH antagonists with add-back, tranexamic acid), myomectomy, embolization or hysterectomy. Types 6–7: laparoscopy if symptomatic. Infertility: resect types 0–2 (ASRM 2017). Anemia: iron. Suspected sarcoma (rapid growth after menopause, heterogeneous, necrosis): contrast MRI with diffusion, avoid uncontained morcellation, gynecologic oncology. Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (Uterus).

novedades.fuentes: ASRM Female Infertility Evaluation (2021) · ATA (2017) · ASRM 2026 · ESHRE POI 2024 · International PMOS Guideline 2023 (Teede)
novedades.texto: Early follicular (2-4): FSH <8-10 optimal, >15 low reserve. LH/FSH>2-3 suggests PCOS. AMH: optimal 1.2-3.5. Mid luteal (day 21): P4 ≥10 optimal. Thyroid: TSH target <2.5. Normal PRL <20-25. ASRM 2026 update: TSH and prolactin only with clinical indication (irregular cycles, galactorrhea, symptoms), not routinely. The LH/FSH ratio is not a diagnostic criterion for PMOS in the 2023 international guideline. Premature ovarian insufficiency (ESHRE 2024): <40 years, oligo/amenorrhea ≥4 months and one FSH >25 IU/L; repeat at 4–6 weeks only if in doubt. Counseling: oocyte donation as a pregnancy option and hormone therapy until the age of natural menopause.

novedades.fuentes: SMFM Consult Series #46 (2018, reaf. 2024) · ISUOG Practice Guidelines (2024, Khalil)
novedades.texto: SMFM #46: mild AFI 24.0-29.9 or DVP 8-11 (65-70% of cases) · moderate AFI 30.0-34.9 or DVP 12-15 (20%) · severe AFI ≥35 or DVP ≥16 (<15%) ISUOG 2024: mild AFI 25-30 · moderate 30.1-35.0 · severe ≥35.1 The greater the severity, the higher the likelihood of an underlying fetal anomaly; severe cases should deliver at a tertiary center (SMFM).

novedades.fuentes: National Library of Medicine. Metformin/Semaglutide/Tirzepatide. Drugs and Lactation Database (LactMed®) · Diab H, Fuquay T, Datta P, Bickel U, Thompson J, Krutsch K. Subcutaneous Semaglutide during Breastfeeding: Infant Safety Regarding Drug Transfer into Human Milk. Nutrients. 2024;16(17):2886 · ZEPBOUND (tirzepatide) injection — Prescribing Information, DailyMed, section 8.2 Lactation · AAP (metformin compatibility with breastfeeding)
novedades.texto: Metformin: compatible with breastfeeding — infant exposure via milk is generally <0.5% of the weight-adjusted maternal dose, with no adverse effects reported (LactMed, updated 15 August 2026; greater caution in newborns, preterm infants, and infants with renal impairment). LactMed also lists a postpartum restart schedule of 500 mg every 12 hours from day one — useful if an immediate postpartum restart is chosen. Semaglutide: in the only dedicated study to date (Diab et al., Nutrients 2024; 8 women, SC doses 0.25-1 mg/week), semaglutide was not detectable in any of the milk samples analyzed after subcutaneous administration. The authors themselves note the data remain limited — long-term follow-up and data on maternal nutrition/milk composition are lacking. LactMed: use only injectable semaglutide during breastfeeding; some oral forms contain salcaprozate sodium, which may enter milk and accumulate in the infant. Tirzepatide: per the Zepbound label (DailyMed, section 8.2), in 11 breastfeeding women after a single 5 mg SC dose, tirzepatide was undetectable in 164 of 171 milk samples; the cumulative amount in the remaining 7 samples represented <0.02% of the administered maternal dose — a reassuring figure, though it comes from a single dose, not continuous use over time. The UK Mounjaro label concludes that tirzepatide "could be considered" during breastfeeding; LactMed advises more caution with newborns and preterm infants. With this data it is no longer accurate to say "dedicated studies are lacking" for semaglutide/tirzepatide in lactation — they do exist, although small and short-term. Still distinguish the real risk of infant exposure (low, per this preliminary data) from the mere convenience of restarting maternal treatment as soon as possible — two distinct considerations that should not be blended when counseling the patient.

novedades.fuentes: ASRM (2020) Testing and interpreting measures of ovarian reserve · POSEIDON (2016) · ESHRE Bologna (2011) · International PMOS Guideline 2023 (Teede)
novedades.texto: AFC: 2–10 mm follicles in both ovaries, transvaginal, early follicular phase. AMH: can be measured on any cycle day; lower on hormonal contraception. Interpretation: low reserve per POSEIDON with AFC <5 or AMH <1.2 ng/mL; Bologna uses AFC <5–7 or AMH <0.5–1.1 ng/mL. High reserve: ≥20 follicles per ovary is the PMOS ovarian morphology criterion (transducer ≥8 MHz). Use (ASRM 2020): they predict oocyte yield after stimulation, not spontaneous pregnancy; they should not be used as a fertility test or to deny treatment. Age is a better predictor. Low reserve at ≥35 years: do not delay workup or treatment. High reserve: higher risk of excessive response to stimulation. Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (Couple workup).

novedades.fuentes: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 217 (2020) · Ubom AE, Vatish M, Barnea ER; FIGO. Int J Gynaecol Obstet 2023;163(Suppl 2):40-50 (doi 10.1002/ijgo.15113) · Cowles et al. (1993)
novedades.texto: Definitions by society: ACOG PB 217 / NICE / FIGO: rupture of membranes before the onset of labor; preterm (PPROM) if before 37 0/7 wk. FASGO consensus: at least 2 h before the onset of labor. Colombian guideline (2015): more than 1 h before the onset of labor. Latency: time from rupture to the onset of labor. Prolonged PROM: more than 24 h. Epidemiology: PPROM in 2-3% of pregnancies and term PROM in 8% (ACOG PB 217). Periviability: 20 0/7-25 6/7 wk. Survival to discharge: 23 wk 23-27%, 24 wk 42-59%, 25 wk 67-76% (ACOG/SMFM OCC No. 6, 2017; data from the USA, England and Australia before 2017). Tabla propia CaVeSal® · Based on: ACOG PB 217 (2020) · FASGO consensus (2018; 2022 update) · Rev Colomb Obstet Ginecol 2015;66(4) · ACOG/SMFM OCC No. 6 (2017). Clinical: clear fluid leakage (>90% reliability if visualized through the cervical os). Non-invasive tests: nitrazine (pH>6.5), ferning (Fern test), vaginal urea/creatinine (adjunct, low cost; cutoffs not standardized; not adopted by ACOG, RCOG, NICE or FIGO guidelines) and biomarkers. PAMG-1 (AmniSure) is the reference non-invasive test in equivocal cases, owing to its higher specificity; IGFBP-1 + AFP (AmnioQuick Duo+) has comparable accuracy. Interpret together with the clinical assessment. Amniocentesis: now reserved for selected cases because it is invasive. Uses: (1) definitive diagnosis of PROM with indigo carmine or fluorescein; (2) subclinical intra-amniotic infection (20-34 wk): glucose, Gram stain, aerobic/anaerobic and mycoplasma cultures; (3) lung maturity — non-invasive alternative: quantusFLM (ultrasound texture analysis of the fetal lung; sensitivity 74-86%, specificity 87-89%; data in PROM are more limited), useful when the timing of delivery is uncertain. ⚠️ Methylene blue CONTRAINDICATED: used in the past, but it causes intestinal atresia, methemoglobinemia and fetal hemolysis. Do not use it. Sources: Clínic/BCNatal PROM protocol · Palacio, PAMG-1/IGFBP-1 meta-analysis · Eleje (AmnioQuick Duo+) · Bonet-Carne, UOG 2015 · Palacio, AJOG 2017.

novedades.titulo: PROM — Latency antibiotic regimens and criteria for delivery
novedades.fuentes: ACOG PB 217 (2020) · MSPyBS Paraguay 2018 · ACOG/NICHD
novedades.texto: Standard (7 days, 24-34 wk): Days 1-2 IV: Ampicillin 2g q6h + Erythromycin 250mg q6h. Days 3-7 oral: Amoxicillin 250mg q8h + Erythromycin 333mg q8h (ACOG PB 217; MSPyBS 2018 uses amoxicillin 500mg). Alternative: Ampicillin 2g IV q6h x48h → Amoxicillin 250mg PO q8h x5d (MSPyBS: 500mg) + Azithromycin 1g PO single dose. ⚠️ Avoid Amoxicillin+Clavulanate (neonatal NEC). Immediate delivery: chorioamnionitis, abruption, fetal distress, established labor, stillbirth.

novedades.fuentes: ACOG PB 217 · FIGO PROM (2021) · SMFM Consult Series #71 (2024) · ACOG Practice Advisory (2025) · PPROMT, Morris et al. Lancet 2016
novedades.texto: Previable (<22-24 wk): offer termination or expectant management, with counseling (SMFM #71, GRADE 1C). Latency antibiotics may be considered from 20 to 23+6 wk (2C) and are recommended from 24 wk (1B). Corticosteroids and MgSO4 only once neonatal resuscitation is planned (1B). Expectant management before 24 wk: maternal morbidity 60.2% vs 33% and severe 12% vs 5% (ACOG 2025). Far from term preterm (24-33+6): expectant, inpatient, complete lung maturation course, neuroprotective MgSO4 if <32 wk, mandatory latency antibiotics, tocolysis restricted to 48h. Late preterm (34-36+6): expectant management or proceed to delivery (ACOG PB 217). PPROMT: no difference in neonatal sepsis (2% vs 3%); immediate delivery had more respiratory distress (8% vs 5%) and more cesareans (26% vs 19%). Expectant until wk 37 only without infection and with close monitoring. Term (≥37): induction within 12-24h.

novedades.fuentes: MSPBS (2022) p. 23 · OMS/WHO (IMC/BMI; anemia 2024) · ACOG/SMFM OCC 11 (2022) · USPSTF (2023) · CDC
novedades.texto: The highest color wins. Green requires all of its criteria: if a data point is missing (age, BMI, Hb, syphilis or HIV), the woman is not classified as green. Red — pregnancy not recommended or should be postponed (one or more): under 20 years · BMI <18.5 or ≥30 · Hb <7 g/dL or intense palmar pallor · exposure to chemicals or radiation · active untreated STI (including HIV, Zika and hepatitis B) · uncontrolled prior disease · alcohol, tobacco or drugs · past or current violence · prior major congenital malformation due to an uncontrolled chronic maternal disease (epilepsy, lupus, diabetes). Management: family planning counseling and postponement, treat or refer, control the prior disease, iron if anemic, albendazole, genetic counseling, violence protocol, STIs according to national protocols. Folic acid 5 mg/day if there is a prior neural tube defect. Yellow — fit to conceive with risk factors (one or more): 35 years or older · BMI 25–29.9 · Hb 7–11.9 g/dL or moderate pallor · controlled prior disease · oral health problems · prior perinatal death, low birth weight, preterm birth or miscarriages · multiple sexual partners without protection · treated STI · prior hypertensive disorder or gestational diabetes, hemorrhage or complications of labor or puerperium · Rh sensitization. Management: iron and folic acid 5 mg/day, albendazole, oral health, lifestyle, breast and cervical cancer prevention, family planning, vaccines. Green — fit to conceive (all): 20 to 34 years · BMI 18.5–24.9 · Hb ≥12 g/dL without pallor · non-reactive syphilis · non-reactive HIV · none of the above criteria. Folic acid 0.4 mg/day and counseling. Folic acid timing: from 3 months before stopping contraception or trying to conceive until the 3rd month of pregnancy (MSPBS); at least 1 month before (USPSTF 2023). Ambiguities in the table and how they were resolved: 1) Age: MSPBS places 35 in green (20 to 35) and in yellow (35 or older); 35 is taken as yellow (ACOG/SMFM Obstetric Care Consensus No. 11, 2022): fertility falls and genetic risk rises. 2) Hemoglobin: MSPBS gives no color between 11 and 12; in non-pregnant women WHO 2024 defines anemia below 12 (mild 11–11.9), so it goes to yellow; the cut-off of 11 applies to pregnant women. 3) BMI: "> 30 or more" is read as 30 or more. ⚠️ Differences with other guidelines: WHO 2024 defines severe anemia below 8 g/dL in non-pregnant women; MSPBS sets red below 7. MSPBS places all obesity in red; WHO divides it into class I (30–34.9), II (35–39.9) and III (≥40). MSPBS gives folic acid 5 mg with any yellow factor; international guidelines reserve the high dose for prior neural tube defect, diabetes, obesity or epilepsy (see Preconception screening and folic acid). TSH is in the laboratory list but not in the traffic light: it is interpreted with the TSH table in the guides (ATA 2017). Laboratory (MSPBS): hemoglobin and hematocrit, blood group and Rh, glucose, urea, creatinine, TSH, lipid profile; rubella, syphilis, toxoplasma, hepatitis B, HIV and Chagas serologies; urinalysis and urine culture; Pap smear. Live-virus vaccines: avoid pregnancy for 3 months. Source: MSPBS, National Manual of Care Standards (2022), p. 23. Adapted table. Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (Preconception).

novedades.fuentes: ACOG PB 197 · ASH 2018 · ACR 2020 · SMFM Consult #64 · ASRM 2026
novedades.texto: Criteria: ≥1 thrombosis or ≥1 obstetric morbidity + confirmed labs on 2 occasions (12 wk apart). Treatment: ASA 100mg/night + prophylactic LMWH from FHR confirmation until 42 days postpartum. Preconception planning (ACR 2020, SMFM #64): obstetric APS without thrombosis: low-dose aspirin + prophylactic heparin in pregnancy and postpartum. Thrombotic APS: therapeutic-dose heparin; switch warfarin to heparin before week 6. Positive antiphospholipid antibodies without clinical criteria: low-dose aspirin. Counseling with maternal-fetal medicine and rheumatology or hematology. Inherited thrombophilias (ACOG PB 197): test only with a personal history of thromboembolism or a first-degree relative with high-risk thrombophilia. Not routine in infertility (ASRM 2026). Do not order MTHFR.

novedades.fuentes: Monash Guideline (Teede et al., 2023) · Rotterdam Consensus (ESHRE/ASRM) · Teede HJ, et al. The Lancet (2026)
novedades.texto: In May 2026, an international consensus of 56 organizations (The Lancet, endorsed by WHO) renamed the condition from "Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)" to "Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS)" — it does not change the diagnostic criteria (Rotterdam/Monash), it better reflects the systemic, metabolic and multi-hormonal nature of the condition. ≥2 of 3: (1) oligo/anovulation · (2) clinical/biochemical hyperandrogenism · (3) PCOM (ultrasound ≥20 follicles or elevated AMH). Phenotypes: A complete · B anovulatory (normal ultrasound) · C ovulatory (PCOM, regular cycles) · D non-androgenic. Applying the criteria (2023 international guideline): with irregular cycles and hyperandrogenism, ultrasound and AMH are not needed. Adolescents: both ovulatory dysfunction and hyperandrogenism are required; do not use ultrasound or AMH until 8 years after menarche. Exclude first: pregnancy, thyroid dysfunction (TSH), hyperprolactinemia, non-classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia (17-OH progesterone) and, as clinically indicated, androgen-secreting tumors or Cushing's. Hirsutism: modified Ferriman-Gallwey ≥4–6 by ethnicity. Biochemical: total or free testosterone (free androgen index). Metabolism: the guideline does not recommend measuring insulin or HOMA-IR in routine practice; order a 75 g OGTT when planning pregnancy. See "Insulin resistance — HOMA-IR and OGTT in PMOS". Fertility: letrozole first line for ovulation induction (2023 guideline, WHO 2025). Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (PMOS).

novedades.fuentes: WHO / CDC / ATA / Cochrane
novedades.texto: Folic acid: 400–800 µg/day standard from preconception. 4 mg/day (ACOG) or 5 mg/day (NICE) up to wk 12 with a previous neural tube defect, epilepsy, obesity or diabetes. With MTHFR: standard folic acid at the same dose (CDC, the only form proven to prevent NTDs; methylfolate does not replace it) Iron: 30–60 mg/day prophylaxis (WHO). Anaemia: 120 mg/day elemental iron until Hb normalises, then prophylaxis. Hb <7 g/dL: IV iron from the 2nd trimester and consider transfusion according to the clinical picture Calcium: requirement 1000 mg/day (1300 under 19 years), the same as outside pregnancy (IOM 2011). WHO: 1.5–2 g/day in low-intake populations to prevent pre-eclampsia. Cochrane 2025 (Cluver, 10 trials, 37,504 women): no difference in pre-eclampsia in the large trials. Physician's decision; separate from iron Vitamin D: 20–29 ng/mL: supplement at the physician's discretion (1000–2000 IU/day); deficiency <20: 2000–4000 IU/day. Without testing: Endocrine Society 2024 suggests empirical supplementation; WHO 2020, no routine supplementation Omega-3 (DHA): 200–300 mg/day in the general population. With risk of preterm birth: 500–1000 mg/day DHA+EPA before 20 wk (Cochrane 2018: 42% fewer births <34 wk) Iodine: 150 µg/day supplement (potassium iodide) from preconception; total intake target 250 µg/day (ATA). Avoid supplements >500 µg/day

novedades.titulo: Ovarian tumor — IOTA rules and O-RADS system
novedades.fuentes: ACR O-RADS US v2022 (Strachowski MJ et al. Radiology 2023) · IOTA (Timmerman et al., 2008/2016) · ESGO/ISUOG/IOTA/ESGE (2021) · ACOG PB 174 · RCOG GTG 62
novedades.texto: IOTA: B (benign) vs. M (malignant) rules — only B=benign, only M=malignant, both/none=inconclusive (ADNEX or expert). O-RADS US v2022: 0 incomplete · 1 physiologic · 2 almost certainly benign (<1%) · 3 low risk (1-<10%) · 4 intermediate (10-<50%) · 5 high (≥50%). v2022 changes: smooth bilocular cyst becomes 2; classic lesions (hemorrhagic, dermoid, endometrioma) managed by size and menopause; color score in smooth solid lesions; ascites or peritoneal nodules = 5. Management by result: O-RADS 2 follow-up by size. O-RADS 3: follow-up in 6 months or gynecologist; if solid, expert ultrasound or MRI. O-RADS 4 or inconclusive IOTA: CA-125 and CEA (CA 19-9 if mucinous; AFP, hCG and LDH if <40), contrast MRI (O-RADS MRI) or expert ultrasound, gynecologist with oncology support. O-RADS 5 or malignant IOTA: same markers, contrast CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis, and referral to gynecologic oncology. Referral (ACOG): postmenopausal CA-125 >35 U/mL, premenopausal >200 U/mL, ascites, fixed or nodular mass, metastasis. HE4 and ROMA as support. Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (Adnexal mass).

novedades.titulo: Ovarian tumors by origin and tumor markers
novedades.fuentes: WHO 2020 (female genital tumours) · ESMO non-epithelial (Ray-Coquard I et al. Ann Oncol 2018;29 Suppl 4:iv1-iv18) · ESGO-ESMO-ESP 2024 · RCOG GTG 62 · ACOG PB 174
novedades.texto: Epithelial (most, especially after 50): high-grade serous → CA-125 (HE4 as support) · low-grade serous → CA-125 · endometrioid and clear cell → CA-125 (HE4) · mucinous → CEA and CA 19-9 (CA-125 often normal); rule out a GI primary · Brenner → no specific marker · borderline → CA-125 or CEA/CA 19-9 by type. Germ cell (girls, adolescents and under 40): dysgerminoma → LDH (hCG if syncytiotrophoblast) · yolk sac tumor → AFP · embryonal carcinoma → AFP and hCG · non-gestational choriocarcinoma → hCG · immature teratoma → AFP sometimes raised · mature teratoma (dermoid) → no marker; CA 19-9 may rise · gonadoblastoma (dysgenetic gonad) → karyotype before surgery in premenarchal girls. Sex cord-stromal: granulosa cell → inhibin B (and inhibin A), AMH, estradiol; may thicken the endometrium · Sertoli-Leydig → testosterone (virilization); AFP sometimes · thecoma → estrogens · fibroma → no marker; with ascites and pleural effusion (Meigs) CA-125 may rise. Metastatic: GI (Krukenberg) → CEA and CA 19-9 · breast → CA 15-3. What each marker measures: CA-125 serous epithelial; also rises with endometriosis, menstruation, pregnancy, PID, fibroids, ascites of any cause, cirrhosis and peritonitis, and is normal in about half of stage I · HE4 epithelial, less affected by endometriosis; ROMA combines CA-125, HE4 and menopause · CEA mucinous and GI; rises with smoking · CA 19-9 mucinous, pancreas and biliary tract, dermoid · AFP yolk sac, embryonal, immature teratoma; also liver and pregnancy · β-hCG choriocarcinoma, embryonal, dysgerminoma with syncytium; always rule out pregnancy and trophoblastic disease · LDH dysgerminoma; nonspecific · inhibin B and AMH granulosa · CA 15-3 breast: follow-up of metastatic disease, not for screening or diagnosis · SCC squamous cervical carcinoma (follow-up). When to order: postmenopausal adnexal mass → CA-125. Under 40 with complex or solid mass → AFP, β-hCG and LDH, plus CA-125. Suspicious mass (O-RADS 4–5, IOTA M) → CA-125 and CEA; CA 19-9 if mucinous; inhibin B if granulosa is suspected. No marker alone distinguishes benign from malignant (ESGO-ESMO-ESP 2024). CaVeSal® original table. Shown in CaVeSal® GYN (Adnexal mass).

novedades.titulo: Violence against women — Where to go and duty to report (Paraguay)
novedades.fuentes: Law No. 5777/2016 (arts. 6, 22, 43, 46, 47) · Decree No. 6973/2017 (arts. 11-13) · Ministry of Women — Line 137 “SOS Mujer”
novedades.texto: Forms of violence (Law 5777, art. 6): femicidal, physical, psychological, sexual, against reproductive rights, patrimonial and economic, workplace, political, intrafamily, obstetric, media, telematic, symbolic, institutional and against dignity. Duty to report: those working in public or private health services who learn of an act of violence against a woman in the course of their work are obliged to file a report (Decree 6973/2017, art. 11). Where to report: National Police (911 or police station), Public Prosecutor’s Office (Fiscalía), Justice of the Peace courts and, for girls or adolescents, Childhood and Adolescence courts (Decree 6973/2017, art. 12). The report may be oral or written, without a lawyer, and cannot be refused; if filed with a non-competent institution, it is redirected within 24 h (Law 5777, art. 47; Decree 6973/2017, art. 13). Support and guidance: Line 137 “SOS Mujer” of the Ministry of Women — free, 24 h, nationwide. Provides psychological support and legal and social advice. It does not take reports: to report, call 911 or go to a police station. Duties of the health service (Law 5777, art. 22): immediately issue a medical certificate and a medical and/or psychological diagnosis to the victim; register the case for the Unified and Standardized Registry System; apply early-detection and care protocols. Protection measures (Law 5777, art. 43): ordered by the Justice of the Peace or the Criminal Guarantees Court — minimum distance, prohibition of harassment or intimidation, police custody, judicial protection and assistance order, among others. Sugerencia CaVeSal® — During the visit: record in the “Violence / Social risk” field what the woman reports, in her own words, and what is observed; inform her of her rights and available resources in understandable language (Law 5777, art. 46).

novedades.titulo: Vitamin D — Tissue associations and supplementation schemes (FLASOG)
novedades.fuentes: Federación Latinoamericana de Sociedades de Obstetricia y Ginecología (FLASOG). Recomendaciones sobre Vitamina D en Salud Reproductiva. Ginecol Obstet Mex. 2026;94:e11309 · Demay MB, Pittas AG, Bikle DD, et al. Vitamin D for the Prevention of Disease: An Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2024
novedades.texto: The vitamin D receptor (VDR) is present in multiple tissues of the reproductive tract and neighboring tissues, underlying the clinical associations described in Table 1 of the FLASOG document: Table 1 — Tissue distribution of the VDR and impact on gyn-obstetric conditions: Ovary and endometrium → PMOS, infertility, endometriosis → proposed mechanism: endometrial receptivity, implantation, insulin sensitivity, inflammatory modulation. Placenta → gestational complications (preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, preterm birth) → placental angiogenesis and maternal-fetal immune tolerance. Vagina, bladder, and urethra → genitourinary syndrome of menopause, recurrent urinary tract infections → vaginal epithelial integrity, collagen synthesis, pH regulation, mucosal immunity. Bone and skeletal muscle → osteosarcopenia, osteoporosis, bone fragility, risk of falls/fractures → bone mineralization, preservation of muscle mass (type II fibers), muscle fat clearance. Pelvic floor musculature → pelvic floor dysfunction, urinary incontinence, pelvic sarcopenia → type II striated muscle fibers, muscle strength. Mammary gland → proliferative conditions → regulation of cell proliferation, local tissue homeostasis. Table 2 — Guiding supplementation schemes (cholecalciferol, unless calcifediol is indicated): Prevention: 1,000-2,000 IU/day — standard maintenance dose. Insufficiency: 2,000 IU/day or 50,000 IU/month — gradual correction. Moderate deficiency: 50,000 IU every 2 weeks × 6-8 weeks — prioritizes comfort and adherence. Severe deficiency (<10 ng/mL): 50,000 IU/week × 6-8 weeks — rapid correction; avoid massive annual/spaced-out doses. Obesity or malabsorption: doses 2-3 times the usual amount, due to lower bioavailability. Clarification — GLP-1/GIP is not the same as malabsorption: use of GLP-1/GIP analogues (semaglutide, tirzepatide — see corresponding guide) is not by itself an indication to raise the Vitamin D dose under the "obesity or malabsorption" scheme above. These drugs slow gastric emptying and reduce intake, but do not create a state of fat/fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption comparable to bariatric surgery (gastric bypass, sleeve with a malabsorptive component), which does justify it. Adjust the Vitamin D dose in a patient on GLP-1/GIP according to her actual nutritional status/serum levels, not automatically because she is on the drug. Cholecalciferol vs. calcifediol: the FLASOG document positions cholecalciferol as the usual first line, reserving calcifediol for scenarios of obesity/malabsorption, liver disease, need for faster correction, or insufficient response to cholecalciferol. Pregnancy: 1,000-2,000 IU/day as the usual scheme; for deficiency requiring more intensive correction, individualize under supervision, not exceeding 4,000 IU/day. Note: the FLASOG document frames the therapeutic goal as reaching "adequate serum 25(OH)D concentrations," without setting a single numeric target range in ng/mL in its text — which is why this guide does not reproduce a single "target" figure (an earlier version used 40-80 ng/mL; it was removed as it was not sourced in this document). The deficiency/insufficiency thresholds are explicit and underlie Table 2 above. ⚠️ Caution note: some educational sources mention experimental very-high-dose protocols (e.g. "Coimbra," 40,000-100,000 IU/day) for autoimmune disease — these protocols are experimental, carry real risk of hypercalcemia/hypercalciuria/kidney stones, and are not endorsed by any formal FLASOG, ACOG, NICE, or USPSTF guideline; they must not be confused with the standard supplementation schemes in this guide. See the next guide for the current controversy over whether population-wide screening (routine 25-OH-D testing) is warranted before prescribing this supplementation.

novedades.fuentes: U.S. Food and Drug Administration. WEGOVY (semaglutide) prescribing information. Revised 2026 · European Medicines Agency. Mounjaro (tirzepatide). Summary of Product Characteristics · Eli Lilly and Company. Mounjaro (tirzepatide) SmPC · U.S. Food and Drug Administration. ZEPBOUND (tirzepatide) prescribing information · Imbroane M, LeMoine K, Nau C, et al. AJOG 2025;233(2):116.e1-e7 · European Medicines Agency. Bydureon (exenatide) SmPC · U.S. Food and Drug Administration. SAXENDA (liraglutide) prescribing information, 2026
novedades.texto: Semaglutide: the 2026 FDA Wegovy label recommends stopping ≥2 months before trying to conceive, due to its prolonged half-life (~1 week, ~5 half-lives for near-complete elimination). This applies to all its presentations (injectable, including the 7.2 mg dose, and tablets). Tirzepatide: here the regulatory agencies differ, and CaVeSal presents both positions without resolving them, so you can decide according to the patient's context: the European label (EMA/Lilly Mounjaro SmPC) recommends stopping ≥1 month before trying to conceive (UK/European label revised 29/08/2026); the U.S. prescribing information (FDA, Zepbound) does not set a mandatory preconception window and instead instructs discontinuing upon recognizing pregnancy — reflecting a genuine difference in regulatory stance, not an error in either source. Tirzepatide elimination half-life: about 5-6 days (FDA label). Liraglutide (daily dosing, half-life about 13 hours): the FDA Saxenda label sets no preconception interval; it instructs stopping when pregnancy is recognized. There is no validated interval; do not use a fixed figure. Extended-release exenatide (weekly): the European Bydureon label (EMA) states it should not be used in pregnancy and should be stopped at least 3 months before a planned pregnancy. Dulaglutide, short-acting exenatide, lixisenatide: the labels of these molecules do not set a specific preconception washout window the way semaglutide/tirzepatide do — the usual instruction is to discontinue upon confirming pregnancy, with no preconception interval validated by dedicated studies. ⚠️ Absence of a validated interval does not mean "no need to stop before trying to conceive" — in the absence of specific data, a prudent approach is to apply a criterion similar to semaglutide (weekly-order half-lives) for dulaglutide (weekly depot); for short-acting exenatide and lixisenatide (daily dosing) there are no specific data. Retatrutide: a triple GLP-1/GIP/glucagon agonist still under investigation — not approved for general clinical use as of this guide (see the Incretin development pipeline guide). It therefore has no indication or label for use in a population seeking pregnancy; any exposure would occur in the context of a clinical trial, with its own study-specific contraception/washout protocol — do not extrapolate the windows above to this molecule. Imbroane et al. (AJOG 2025;233(2):116.e1-e7; n=4,267 per cohort after matching, 8,534 total) found, in their retrospective preconception cohort (TriNetX), an association with lower incidence of gestational diabetes (18.2% vs. 15.2%; OR 0.81; 95% CI 0.72-0.91), hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (22.8% vs. 19.9%; OR 0.84; 95% CI 0.76-0.94), preterm delivery (4.4% vs. 3.0%; OR 0.68; 95% CI 0.54-0.85), and cesarean delivery (19.7% vs. 17.6%; OR 0.89; 95% CI 0.87-0.97) in the group with prior GLP-1/GIP prescription versus the unexposed group. ⚠️ Before matching, the exposed group had a much higher prevalence of overweight/obesity (76.8% vs. 10.7%), type 2 diabetes (37.6% vs. 1.5%), hypertension (32.5% vs. 3.7%), and prior GDM (25.3% vs. 10.0%) — matching adjusted only for age/race/ethnicity/comorbidity categories, not finely for these factors, so much of this apparent protection may reflect residual confounding by indication (who receives GLP-1/GIP) rather than a true protective drug effect. This does not change this guide's preconception washout recommendation — see also the Inadvertent pregnancy during GLP-1/tirzepatide guide for a contrasting read on maternal metabolic/hypertensive outcomes.

novedades.texto: Finding Interpretation and management Absent nasal bone Absent in ~60–70% of T21. In euploid fetuses: 2.2% in Caucasian, 5% in Asian and 9% in Afro-Caribbean women; falls with CRL (4.7% at 45–54 mm, 1% at 75–84 mm) and rises with NT (Cicero 2004). Integrate with NT and other markers. Ductus venosus with absent or reversed a-wave Marker of aneuploidy and congenital heart disease. Refer to Fetal Medicine, echocardiography. Tricuspid regurgitation Associated with T21 and congenital heart disease. Fetal echocardiography. Choroid plexus cyst(s) Soft marker, more associated with T18 than T21. Isolated with normal screening: low residual risk. 2 or more abnormal findings Increased chromosomal risk: refer to Fetal Medicine for genetic counselling; NIPT or invasive testing (CVS 11–13+6 wk) according to informed choice.

novedades.texto: MSPBS 2018 Criterion Management Low risk Bile acids 10–19 µmol/L with normal enzymes Outpatient, weekly tests; elective delivery at 36–37 wk Moderate risk Bile acids 20–39 and/or AST/ALT raised up to twice normal ≥28 wk: admission, tests every 72 h; if no response, manage as high risk. Delivery 36–37 wk (CaVeSal® suggestion: the manual sets no week for this group) High risk Bile acids ≥40 and/or enzymes >2× and/or no response to treatment Always admit. <34 wk: UDCA at maximum dose; if no improvement, lung maturation and delivery. ≥36 wk: deliver National criterion (Paraguay): Manual Nacional de Normas de Atención de las Principales Patologías Obstétricas (MSPBS/SPGO 2018), ch. 5. Diagnosis: itching + bile acids ≥10 µmol/L and/or raised enzymes or bilirubin. UDCA 10–16 mg/kg/day in 2 doses (start 900 mg/day, maximum 1200 mg/day). Follow-up: liver profile, bile acids and PT every 1–2 wk; CTG every 3–7 days. Regional reference (MINSAL Chile 2015): anicteric 38 wk; icteric (bilirubin >1.2 + raised enzymes) 36 wk. International reference (RCOG GTG 43, 2022): diagnosis ≥19 µmol/L; 19–39 birth by 40 wk; 40–99 38–39 wk; ≥100 35–36 wk. With ≥100, consider earlier delivery. In all cases: deliver if fetal wellbeing is compromised, regardless of GA.

novedades.titulo: Management when the entered data are normal
novedades.fuentes: CaVeSal® suggestion · Based on: ESHRE 2022 · FIGO · MSPBS Paraguay · SMFM Consult Series #74 (2025) · ACOG Practice Advisory (2026) · ACOG CO 797 (2020) · CDC/ACIP · ISUOG · WHO (calcium) · Dwarkanath P et al. NEJM 2024
novedades.texto: Calculate button: every entered item returns a result and a management step, also when normal. If a test is already entered its result is used; if it is missing and needed, it is suggested. Labs within range: summary of the normal values. Repeat according to the Lab schedule. Fasting glucose <92 mg/dL before 24 wk: 75 g OGTT at 24–28 wk. Non-reactive serologies (HIV, syphilis, HBsAg, hepatitis C, Chagas): repeat according to the Lab schedule. Anti-HBs negative: not immune to hepatitis B; the vaccine is safe in pregnancy, give it if HBsAg is negative. CMV IgG negative: susceptible; hygiene measures (hand washing after changing diapers, do not share utensils with young children). Group B streptococcus negative: no intrapartum prophylaxis; the result is valid for 5 weeks. Recurrent pregnancy loss (2 or more miscarriages): antiphospholipid work-up (lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin, anti-β2 glycoprotein I), TSH and anti-TPO, early follow-up. Grand multiparity (5 or more births/caesareans): higher risk of postpartum haemorrhage and malpresentation; birth plan with active management of the third stage. 2 or more caesareans: planned repeat caesarean per MSPBS Paraguay; if she arrives in the second stage, manage as one previous caesarean. Normal 1st-trimester screening: scan without markers, low combined risk or low-risk cell-free DNA: anomaly scan at 20–22 wk. Age ≥35 with scan only: offer cell-free DNA or combined test. If screening is already entered, the age card does not request it again. Anomaly scan without anomalies: 3rd-trimester growth according to overall risk; suggests cervical length and 2T uterine PI if not recorded. Fetal weight: P10–P89, appropriate growth. P3–P10 without Doppler: request Doppler (UA, MCA/CPR, uterine) to distinguish SGA from FGR. Supplementation: prophylactic iron 30–60 mg/day with normal Hb (WHO); with MTHFR, standard folic acid (methylfolate optional); vitamin D according to the entered value; calcium at the physician's discretion (WHO in low intake vs. Cochrane 2025 no effect on pre-eclampsia); see Supplementation in pregnancy.

novedades.fuentes: CaVeSal® own table · Based on: WHO (iron and folic acid; calcium) · CDC · IOM 2011 · Cluver CA et al. Cochrane 2025 · Dwarkanath P et al. NEJM 2024 · ATA 2017 · Middleton P et al. Cochrane 2018
novedades.texto: Folic acid: 0.4–0.8 mg/day from preconception to at least 12 wk. High dose with a previous NTD (previous pregnancy, or the woman or her partner with an NTD), epilepsy or antiseizure drugs, obesity or diabetes: 4 mg/day (ACOG PB 187, CDC) or 5 mg/day (NICE, RCOG), from 3 months before conception to 12 wk; then return to the standard dose. Another previous malformation does not justify it. In Obstetric history, the “Previous NTD” box activates the high dose. MTHFR: folic acid remains the standard (CDC), as it is the only form proven to prevent NTDs. Methylfolate (5-MTHF) 400–800 µg/day is an optional alternative. Iron: prophylaxis 30–60 mg/day elemental iron (WHO). Anaemia: 120 mg/day until Hb normalises, then back to prophylaxis. Hb <7 g/dL: IV iron from the 2nd trimester and consider transfusion according to the clinical picture. Calcium: requirement 1000 mg/day (1300 under 19 years), the same as outside pregnancy. WHO: 1.5–2 g/day in 3 doses in low-intake populations. Cochrane 2025 (10 trials, 37,504 women): no difference in pre-eclampsia in the large trials. Physician's decision; separate from iron. Iodine: 150 µg/day supplement (potassium iodide) from preconception; total intake target 250 µg/day. Avoid supplements >500 µg/day and seaweed. Omega-3: with risk of preterm birth, 500–1000 mg/day DHA+EPA before 20 wk (Cochrane 2018: 42% fewer births <34 wk). Effect on pre-eclampsia uncertain. Vitamin D: see the vitamin D section in this tab.

novedades.fuentes: Table adapted (translated) from Alexander EK et al. ATA 2017 · CaVeSal® suggestion · Based on: ATA 2011 · Endocrine Society 2012 · ETA 2014 · Lazarus JH et al. NEJM 2012 · Casey BM et al. NEJM 2017
novedades.texto: Use the laboratory pregnancy range. If not reported: TSH upper limit 4.0 µIU/mL (ATA 2017; the trimester no longer changes the cutoff). Check anti-TPO if TSH is >2.5 in the 1st trimester (ATA 2017, rec. 28) or >3.0 in the 2nd–3rd (CaVeSal® suggestion). Anti-TPO TSH (µIU/mL) Levothyroxine Anti-TPO+ >4.0 (above range) Recommended Anti-TPO+ 2.5–4.0 Consider Anti-TPO− ≥10 Recommended Anti-TPO− 4.0–10 Consider Anti-TPO− <4.0 Do not treat Grey zone (CaVeSal® suggestion): TSH >2.5 in T1 or >3.0 in T2–T3 and ≤4.0: check anti-TPO; if positive, consider levothyroxine. History of the cutoffs: ATA 2011 and Endocrine Society 2012: 2.5 / 3.0 / 3.0 by trimester. ETA 2014: 2.5 / 3.0 / 3.5. ATA 2017 replaced them with the laboratory range or 4.0. Trials: CATS (Lazarus 2012, 21,846 women, treatment at ~13 weeks: IQ at 3 years 99.2 vs 100.0) and Casey (2017, TSH ≥4.0, treatment at ~17 weeks: IQ at 5 years 97 vs 94) showed no neurodevelopmental benefit. The link between high TSH and cognitive deficit is observational. Preconception: treated hypothyroid women, TSH between the lower limit and 2.5. IVF/ICSI with subclinical hypothyroidism: levothyroxine with a TSH goal <2.5 (ATA 2017, rec. 20). Low TSH in T1: may be physiological due to hCG; confirm with free T4 and, if Graves disease is suspected, TRAb. Low free T4 with normal TSH: isolated hypothyroxinemia; not routinely treated. Free T4 varies by method and trimester.

novedades.fuentes: Based on: Grobman WA et al. (NICHD) 2007 · MSPBS Paraguay · FIGO 2025 · ACOG · RCOG · RANZCOG
novedades.texto: Candidate: one previous caesarean with a low transverse scar. Favour success: previous vaginal birth and non-recurrent previous indication. Assess carefully: potentially recurrent previous indication; previous uterine surgery according to myometrial extent. Absolute contraindication: classical or inverted-T scar. Two or more caesareans: planned repeat caesarean per MSPBS Paraguay (vaginal birth is discouraged; uterine rupture ~1.4 %). If she arrives in the second stage: manage as one previous caesarean. International view: ACOG, RCOG and RANZCOG allow vaginal birth after 2 caesareans with senior obstetrician counselling; FIGO is more restrictive. With 3 or more, evidence is very limited. The Calculator estimates the probability of success with the Grobman score. Requirements: immediate surgical availability and informed consent; discuss the risk of uterine rupture (0.5–0.9 %). Misoprostol is contraindicated.

Ultrasound signs (ISUOG 2016): loss of the retroplacental clear zone, placental lacunae, myometrial thinning <1 mm, disruption of the bladder line, placental bulge, focal exophytic mass; Doppler: uterovesical or subplacental hypervascularity and bridging vessels. novedades.seccion: Mode of Delivery — Robson, Bishop, Biometry
novedades.fuentes: CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: sources listed for each group · PAHO/WHO — Robson Classification (2018).
novedades.texto: Group Management Sources 1 Prolonged latent phase and slow but progressive labor are not indications for cesarean. Partograph according to the chosen model (Ministry CLAP from 4 cm, WHO 2020 from 5 cm, ACOG from 6 cm). Active-phase arrest: ≥6 cm with ruptured membranes and no change with ≥4 h of adequate contractions or ≥6 h of oxytocin with inadequate contractions. Second stage: ≥3 h of pushing before diagnosing arrest (longer with epidural, individualized). Continuous support. WHO — Labour Care Guide 2020 · ACOG/SMFM — Safe prevention of the primary cesarean delivery (2014) 2a / 4a Induce only with a clear indication; from 41+0 weeks induction is recommended. Bishop ≤6: cervical ripening (oral misoprostol 25 µg q2h or vaginal 25 µg q6h, balloon, or balloon + oxytocin). Do not diagnose failed induction in the latent phase before ≥24 h of induction and ≥12-18 h of oxytocin after membrane rupture. Never unsupervised; induce where an operating room is available. WHO — Induction of labour at or beyond term (2022) · WHO — Induction of labour (2011) · WHO — Mechanical methods (2022) · ACOG/SMFM — Safe prevention of the primary cesarean delivery (2014) 2b / 4b Verify and document the indication. Without a medical indication, do not schedule before 39 weeks. ACOG CO 765 (2019) · ACOG/SMFM — Safe prevention of the primary cesarean delivery (2014) 3 Same criteria as Group 1 with multiparous standards. Second stage: ≥2 h of pushing. Lowest cesarean rate group: a cesarean here deserves review of the indication. WHO — Labour Care Guide 2020 · ACOG/SMFM — Safe prevention of the primary cesarean delivery (2014) 5.1 VBAC if: low transverse (or low vertical) incision, no previous rupture and no contraindication to vaginal birth. Contraindicated: classical cesarean, T or J incision, previous rupture. Only with 24-h emergency cesarean, blood bank and NICU. Continuous fetal monitoring and one-to-one care (abnormal FHR is the most common sign of rupture). Induction with mechanical methods; misoprostol contraindicated; oxytocin with caution. Epidural not contraindicated. Interval under 18 months: higher risk. EFW >4500 g: cesarean (FIGO). FIGO — VBAC (2025) · ACOG PB 205 (2019) · RCOG GTG 45 · WHO — Induction of labour (2011) 5.2 MSPBS Paraguay: with 2 or more cesareans, planned repeat cesarean from 39 weeks; vaginal birth is discouraged (uterine rupture ~1.4%). If she arrives in the second stage, manage as one previous cesarean. International view: with two cesareans, FIGO generally does not recommend VBAC (only with a previous vaginal birth, senior obstetrician counseling and a high-complexity center); RCOG and ACOG allow it with counseling. Three or more: insufficient data on VBAC (ACOG PB 205); cesarean is usually scheduled. With placenta previa or low anterior placenta, rule out accreta. MSPBS Paraguay — Obstetric conditions · FIGO — VBAC (2025) · ACOG PB 205 (2019) · RCOG GTG 45 6 Offer external cephalic version (ECV) from 36 weeks. Without ECV: planned cesarean from 39 weeks, or vaginal breech birth only with an institutional protocol, trained operator and written consent. In labor: ultrasound (type of breech, head flexion, EFW) and continuous monitoring; inadequate progress → cesarean. Imminent delivery: hands-off assistance. ACOG CO 745 (2018, reaf. 2023) · RCOG GTG 20b 7 Same as Group 6, with ECV from 37 weeks. With one previous low transverse cesarean, ECV may be attempted if she is a good VBAC candidate. ACOG CO 745 (2018, reaf. 2023) · RCOG GTG 20b · FIGO — VBAC (2025) 8 Uncomplicated dichorionic or monochorionic diamniotic twins, >32 weeks, first twin cephalic, no significant discordance: vaginal birth and cesarean are equally safe. First twin non-cephalic: cesarean. Monoamniotic: cesarean (32+0-33+6). Triplets: cesarean. One previous low transverse cesarean does not contraindicate VBAC. Active third stage due to higher hemorrhage risk. NICE NG137 (2019) · ACOG PB 231 (2021) · ACOG/SMFM — Safe prevention of the primary cesarean delivery (2014) · FIGO — VBAC (2025) 9 In labor or with ruptured membranes: cesarean (cord prolapse, uterine rupture). Before labor and without contraindications: ECV from 37 weeks. Ultrasound to rule out a mechanical cause (placenta previa, fibroids, anomalies). With back down, consider a vertical uterine incision. GLOWM · StatPearls — ECV 10 Lung maturation, neuroprotection, tocolysis and PROM according to the preterm labor and PROM cards in this guide. Notify neonatology. Prematurity alone does not determine the mode of birth; it is decided by obstetric conditions. ACOG CO 831 (2021) CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: sources listed for each group · PAHO/WHO — Robson Classification (2018). Fetal lung maturation, magnesium sulfate neuroprotection, tocolysis and PROM follow the management already set in their cards in this guide and in the calculator. Does not replace clinical judgment.

novedades.texto: Placenta accreta spectrum (PAS: accreta/increta/percreta). Main risk factor: prior cesarean plus anterior placenta previa/low-lying placenta. ⚠️ Golden rule: whenever signs of accreta are present, never attempt manual placental removal — leave the placenta in situ and proceed to en bloc hysterectomy, at a Level III-IV center, with a planned cesarean at 34+0-35+6 weeks. Risk factors: number of prior cesareans, prior uterine curettage, prior uterine surgery (myomectomy), history of Asherman syndrome — in addition to placenta previa/low-lying placenta and maternal age >35 or IVF, already recorded under Morphology and History. 2D ultrasound signs: loss of the clear zone, myometrial thinning (<1mm), irregular placental lacunae ("Swiss cheese" appearance), interruption of the bladder-uterine interface, placental bulging toward the bladder, focal exophytic mass. Color Doppler signs: uterovesical and subplacental hypervascularity, bridging vessels, lacunar feeder vessels, parametrial involvement. FIGO Classification (surgical/histopathological confirmation): Grade 1 (Accreta) · Grade 2 (Increta) · Grade 3a (Percreta limited to the uterine serosa) · Grade 3b (Percreta with urinary bladder invasion) · Grade 3c (Percreta with invasion of other pelvic tissues/organs: broad ligament, vaginal wall, pelvic sidewall or any other pelvic organ, with or without bladder invasion). Jauniaux E, et al. FIGO, Int J Gynecol Obstet 2019;146:20-24. ⚠️ Probability and Extent are calculated using the "CaVeSal Classification" — a proprietary scoring scheme developed by the team (not a published FIGO/ISUOG/ACOG score) that combines risk factors + 2D signs + Doppler signs. The FIGO Classification is a separate data point, based on surgical/histopathological confirmation — it does not replace, and should not be confused with, the CaVeSal Classification. Antenatal diagnosis (WAPM/PMF 2026): cesarean scar pregnancy is a potential precursor of PAS — after a previous cesarean, early transvaginal ultrasound to establish the implantation site. In the 2nd-3rd trimester, combined transabdominal and transvaginal ultrasound (placental location, myometrial thickness and contour, uterovesical interface); markers: lacunae, placental bulge, uterovesical hypervascularity and bridging vessels, alone or combined. 2D ultrasound with color Doppler is the mainstay; MRI is complementary (inconclusive ultrasound, non-anterior or non-previa placenta, technical limits). If cesarean scar pregnancy or PAS is suspected: refer to a perinatal center with a multidisciplinary team, blood products, adult and neonatal ICU and complex pelvic surgery; delivery timing is individualized.

High risk — bile acids ≥40 and/or enzymes >2× (>80 IU/L) and/or no response → always admit; <34 wk: UDCA up to maximum dose and, if no improvement, lung maturation and delivery; ≥36 wk: deliver. Regional reference (MINSAL Chile 2015): anicteric → 38 wk · icteric (bilirubin >1.2 + enzymes) → 36 wk. International reference (RCOG 2022): diagnosis ≥19 μmol/L · 40–99 → 38–39 wk · ≥100 → 35–36 wk (consider earlier). Treatment: ursodeoxycholic acid 10–16 mg/kg/day in 2 doses (start 900 mg/day, maximum 1200 mg/day) + vitamin K if cholestasis is prolonged. Follow-up: liver profile, bile acids and PT every 1–2 wk; CTG every 3–7 days. ⚠️ Deliver at any sign of fetal compromise, regardless of pathway or GA.

novedades.titulo: Fezolinetant and elinzanetant — NK receptor antagonists, non-hormonal therapy for vasomotor symptoms
novedades.fuentes: Pratt MC, et al. Expert Rev Clin Pharmacol 2023;16(5):389-398 · Panay N, et al. Climacteric 2024;27(3):221-235 · ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 13. Obstet Gynecol. 2026;148(5):e345-e364 (Table 2) · Qaseem A, et al. ACP. Ann Intern Med 2026. doi:10.7326/ANNALS-26-01205
novedades.texto: Mechanism: neurokinin receptor antagonists that act on hypothalamic KNDy neurons involved in thermoregulation, with no hormonal action. Fezolinetant: selective NK3 antagonist. Elinzanetant: dual NK1/NK3 antagonist. Fezolinetant: 45mg PO once daily, with or without food. FDA-approved for vasomotor symptoms (VMS). ⚠️ FDA boxed warning: requires baseline liver function testing, repeated monthly during the first 3 months of use, and again at 6 and 9 months. Elinzanetant: 120mg PO once daily. FDA-approved for VMS and also for menopause-related sleep disturbance (a sleep benefit not included in fezolinetant's specific approval). Requires liver function testing before starting and again at 3 months of treatment — a less intensive monitoring cadence than fezolinetant. Indication (both): moderate-to-severe VMS of the climacteric, a non-hormonal alternative when HRT is contraindicated or not the patient's preference (hormone-dependent cancer history, VTE, personal preference). In indirect network comparisons (ACOG CPG13), both drugs show similar efficacy on VMS frequency and severity; elinzanetant showed a greater effect on sleep disturbance (PROMIS sleep disturbance score) in indirect comparison with fezolinetant. Most common adverse effects vs. placebo in the OASIS trials with elinzanetant: headache and fatigue. Place in treatment (ACP 2026): 3rd line (moderate certainty), after HRT and SNRIs (desvenlafaxine or venlafaxine), alongside SSRIs and gabapentin. See MRS Scale and Hormone Replacement Therapy.

novedades.titulo: Abnormal uterine bleeding — Surgical indications by cause
novedades.fuentes: ACOG (2013) · ACOG PB 228 · Oderkerk TJ, et al. MIRA2. Lancet 2026;408:1828-1838
novedades.texto: Criteria: stability, severity, failed medical treatment, fertility desire. Fibroid: myomectomy/RFA/embolization/hysterectomy. Adenomyosis: hysterectomy if fertility not desired. Polyps: polypectomy. Severe acute: D&C. Endometrial ablation: alternative, ends fertility. Ablation + LNG-IUS (MIRA2, Lancet 2026): in 715 women under 60 with heavy menstrual bleeding, inserting a 52mg LNG-IUS immediately after ablation reduced hysterectomy at 2 years (4% vs. 10%; RR 0.43), with no more serious adverse events (8% vs. 8%).
